key: And he looked behind him and saw them, and cursed them in the name of the LORD. And there came forth two she-bears out of the wood, and tore forty and two children of them.
s: Mocked by Beth-el’s children, Elisha curses them and bears maul forty-two; Radak, on 2:24, explains that the sages, troubled by the deaths, gave reasons, as that he saw no trace of a commandment in them or their seed, and said he was punished with illness.

evidence.gloss: [Radak on 2:24, on ‘and he saw them and cursed them’:] Our sages differed over this, for it was hard for them how he brought death upon them for such a thing … and some of them said he saw in them no trace of a commandment, nor would there be, neither in them nor in their seed, therefore he cursed them to remove them from the world; and it is said that he was punished for causing the death of these youths, and they said Elisha suffered three illnesses, one for setting bears on children.

reason: verse.js ok, ref 2 Kings 2:24 and at [310,24] match. Radak’s own Hebrew on 2:24 carries the reading: the sages found the deaths hard and gave several reasons, one that he saw no trace of a commandment in them or their seed, and Elisha was punished with one of three illnesses for it. Corrected the sentence in two places: the proposal gave Radak ‘no good in them’, which is Rashi’s and Metzudat David’s wording (לחלוחית טובה); Radak’s is לחלוחית מצוה, so now ‘no trace of a commandment in them or their seed’; and the plain sense now says ‘children’ as the JPS passage does (2:23 ‘little children’), with ‘troubled by the deaths’ and ‘said he was punished with illness’ keeping it within 45 words. Plain sense states the hard event in one plain clause (rule 6); the reading carries the limit Radak reports. entry-check ok on scratch/V-d117-p.json.
